title: Second Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19
what_it_is: Second Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19

sections.label: Circuit breaker and community cases
sections.summary: Community cases rose from nine a day in March to 31 before circuit breaker measures began on 7 April 2020, then fell to 11 last week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: At the same time, we have seen a rise in community cases from nine a day in March, to 31 a day on average in the week before circuit breaker, with an increasing proportion of unlinked cases, suggesting that there is underlying community transmission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We decided to do the hard thing – to impose circuit breaker measures from 7 April 2020, and introduced stricter measures following that on 21 April 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also extended the circuit breaker measures to 1 June 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The average number of new community cases had fallen from 31 in the week before the circuit breaker, to 11 last week.

sections.label: Isolation beds increase
sections.summary: Isolation beds increased from around 550 in January to close to 1,500 as of 2 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our number of isolation beds has increased from around 550 in January this year, to close to 1,500 as of 2 May 2020.

sections.label: Public hospitals ICU bed plans
sections.summary: Public hospitals plan to add another 450 ICU beds by mid-May if needed, with infrastructure, equipment, medications and manpower in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The public hospitals have put in place plans to ensure that their infrastructure, equipment, medications and manpower are in place to add another 450 ICU beds by mid-May if needed.

sections.label: CCF beds for patients
sections.summary: There are currently more than 10,000 beds in the CCFs for patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Currently, we have more than 10,000 beds in our CCFs for our patients.

sections.label: CRF capacity expansion
sections.summary: Patients past day 14 of illness can be transferred to CRFs; around 2,000 CRF bed spaces exist now, expanding to more than 10,000 by end June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Hence, patients past their day 14 of illness can be safely transferred to the CRFs before they are assessed for discharge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We currently have around 2,000 CRF bed spaces, with some of them within our dormitories and others in selected SAF camps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will be expanding CRF capacity to more than 10,000 beds by end June.

sections.label: Circuit breaker measures continue
sections.summary: The rest of the circuit breaker measures will continue to apply till 1 June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The rest of the circuit breaker measures will continue to apply till 1 June.

sections.label: Community cases target
sections.summary: Community cases should ideally fall to zero or single digit daily, sustained over time, with very low unlinked cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Community cases should ideally fall to zero or single digit daily, with very low numbers of unlinked cases and not just for one day but sustained over a period of time.

sections.label: COVID-19 testing numbers
sections.summary: Over 140,000 COVID-19 tests have been conducted, or 2,500 tests per 100,000 people in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To date, we have conducted over 140,000 tests for COVID-19, or 2,500 tests per 100,000 people in Singapore.

sections.label: PCR testing capacity increase
sections.summary: Capacity is over 8,000 PCR tests a day, up from 2,900 in early April, with plans to increase to 40,000 a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Currently, we have the capacity to conduct more than 8,000 PCR tests a day in total across our community and migrant workers in the dormitories, up from 2,900 a day in early April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are working with various private and public sector partners to progressively increase our testing capacity further to up to 40,000 a day.

sections.label: Antibody study findings
sections.summary: A study found none of close to 2,000 samples had antibodies, while around 2.5% of close contacts had antibodies without symptoms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Their study was published last week and found that among close to 2,000 samples from our healthcare workers, volunteers and general population, none had antibodies pointing to a past infection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The study also showed that among close contacts, around 2.5% had antibodies despite not having had symptoms during their quarantine.

sections.label: Testing in senior homes
sections.summary: Testing of staff and residents has started at MOH and MSF Homes with a high proportion of seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As mentioned, we have started to test staff and residents at MOH and MSF Homes with a high proportion of seniors such as nursing homes and welfare homes.

sections.label: Contact tracing teams
sections.summary: 50 contact tracing teams have been set up, up from 20 since the March update, to ringfence and prevent further spread.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This will allow us to quickly ringfence and prevent further spread.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have set up 50 contact tracing teams, up from 20 since my last update in March.

sections.label: COVID-19 cases among healthcare workers
sections.summary: As of 26 April 2020, there were 66 confirmed COVID-19 cases among healthcare workers, 46 of whom had direct patient contact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As of 26 April 2020, there were 66 cases of confirmed COVID-19 infections among healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Forty six cases were from healthcare workers whose work involved direct contact with patients.

sections.label: Special bonus for frontline healthcare workers
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister had previously announced a special bonus for public healthcare workers working on the frontline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister had previously announced a special bonus for our public healthcare workers working on the frontline.

sections.label: Augmenting public healthcare workforce
sections.summary: MOH gave institutions flexibility to deploy staff across institutions and tapped external sources, with over 11,000 SG Healthcare Corps sign-ups as of 3 May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To address these sustainability concerns, MOH has given the public healthcare institutions some flexibility to deploy staff across institutions to meet pressing operational needs on the ground and to support one another as one public healthcare system, with strict infection control protocols in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH has also looked to external sources to augment our public healthcare workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This includes tapping on healthcare professionals in the private sector and encouraging retired and non-practicing staff to return to public practice through the newly launched SG Healthcare Corps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As of 3 May, we received more than 11,000 sign-ups altogether.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I am heartened by this overwhelming response from Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: So far, we have matched about 800 Corps members to various needs on the ground, and they are being progressively deployed and we will do more.

sections.label: Dengue cases in 2020
sections.summary: The total number of dengue cases in 2020 has exceeded 6,000, more than double the same period in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The total number of dengue cases in 2020 has exceeded 6,000 – more than double that over the same period in 2019.

sections.label: Calibrated moves against resurgence
sections.summary: Calibrated moves, key enablers and safeguards are needed to prevent a resurgence as circuit breaker measures are rolled back and Singapore re-opens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We must make calibrated moves to prevent a resurgence of cases and clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We must put in place key enablers and safeguards to allow us to contain the spread and care for future cases, even as we roll back our circuit breaker measures and re-open.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We must remain vigilant and not let our guards down.

sections.label: Outbreak among migrant workers in dormitories
sections.summary: Efforts are being made to control the serious outbreak among migrant workers in the dormitories and to take care of these workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we are doing all we can to control the serious outbreak amongst migrant workers in the dormitories, and to take care of these workers.

sections.label: Worker movement and dormitories
sections.summary: Movement of workers in and out of all dormitories was stopped, and construction workers living outside dormitories were put on a stay-home requirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To minimise the risks of spread to the wider community, we have stopped the movement of workers in and out of all dormitories, and put the construction workers living outside the dormitories on a stay-home requirement.

sections.label: Circuit breaker implementation and extension
sections.summary: The circuit breaker was implemented on 7 April, tightened on 21 April, and extended to 1 June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The second major front is in suppressing the spread of the virus in the community, through the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We implemented the circuit breaker on 7 April; two weeks later, on 21 April, we tightened the circuit breaker measures, and also extended it to 1 June.

sections.label: Infection numbers and easing measures
sections.summary: Daily infection numbers have come down but are not yet single digits, so tightened measures were extended to 11 May with gradual easing after, while key circuit breaker measures largely remain till 1 June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through our collective efforts, we are now seeing some results – daily infection numbers have started to come down, although they are not yet at single digits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we extended the tightened measures for another week till 11 May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Thereafter, we will allow some gradual easing, as we had announced over the weekend, but the key circuit breaker measures will largely remain till 1 June.

sections.label: Masks during strenuous exercise
sections.summary: Requiring people to wear a mask during strenuous exercise is not advisable because it can pose a health risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Requiring people to wear a mask when engaging in strenuous exercise is not advisable because it can pose a health risk.

sections.label: Outdoor exercise allowed with distancing
sections.summary: Prohibiting outdoor exercise altogether can be harmful, so outdoor exercise alone in one's own neighbourhood was allowed so long as safe distancing is in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On the other hand, prohibiting outdoor exercise altogether and keeping people cooped up at home for a long time can be harmful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, on balance, we decided to allow outdoor exercise by yourself, in your own neighbourhood, so long as safe distancing is in place.

sections.label: Isolation at home and circuit breaker
sections.summary: Being isolated at home for long periods is not good for health and well-being, so the circuit breaker was considered carefully before being implemented and later extended for a month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Being isolated at home for long periods is also not good for their health and overall well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why we considered very carefully before we decided to implement the circuit breaker and then later to extend it for a month.

sections.label: Unity Resilience Solidarity Budgets support
sections.summary: The Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets supported businesses, workers and Singaporeans with over $60 billion, including national reserves with the President's permission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To mitigate the impact, we supported businesses, workers and Singaporeans at large with the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets – more than $60 billion in total, including drawing on our national reserves with the President's permission.

sections.label: One address change during circuit breaker
sections.summary: One change of address is allowed during the circuit breaker period for care-giving needs, such as parents moving in with children's grandparents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where possible, and where we assess the risks to be low, we will consider easing and allowing some flexibility on the ground.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to Mr Henry Kwek's question, we do allow one change of address during the circuit breaker period, for care-giving needs, such as for parents to move in with their children's grandparents through that circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Construction productivity and migrant workers
sections.summary: Progress has been made in construction productivity, but there are still 270,000 migrant workers in this sector alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have made progress in construction productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But there are still 270,000 migrant workers in this sector alone.

sections.label: Telecommuting default and safe management
sections.summary: Telecommuting will be a default option extended to all staff, and those who cannot telecommute will have strict safe management practices implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, telecommuting will have to be a default option extended to all staff and for those who cannot telecommute, strict safe management practices will have to be implemented.

sections.label: Reopening starts with critical industries
sections.summary: Reopening will start with industries critical to the economy, local employment and global supply chains, while some sectors like entertainment outlets will wait longer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When we do so, we will start with industries that are critical to the economy and to local employment and that keep us connected to the world and global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Some sectors will have to wait for a bit more time, for example, entertainment outlets or activities that attract crowds or people in close contact with one another.

sections.label: Community surveillance and priority testing
sections.summary: More extensive community surveillance will detect unlinked cases, and testing will prioritise higher risk groups like nursing home residents, staff and healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will involve more extensive community surveillance, so that we are better able to detect any unlinked cases in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also prioritise the testing of higher risk and more vulnerable groups, like the residents and staff of nursing homes and welfare homes as well as healthcare workers that have high touch-points with the community.

sections.label: Testing and contact tracing strategies
sections.summary: Expanded testing and faster contact tracing are the two key strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Expanded testing and faster contact tracing are our two key strategies.

sections.label: Safe resumption of activities
sections.summary: With enablers and safeguards, a safe and gradual resumption of activities in June can be planned if community numbers continue to decline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These are basic fundamentals that we all have to uphold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But with these enablers and the safeguards in place, we can then plan for a safe and gradual resumption of activities in June – provided, as we said just now, we see a continued decline in our community numbers.

sections.label: SGUnited portal donations increase
sections.summary: The SGUnited portal saw a seven-fold increase in total donations compared to the previous year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our SGUnited portal saw a seven-fold increase in the total donations in this period compared to the previous year.

sections.label: Community Care Facilities setup
sections.summary: Community Care Facilities were set up quickly at the Singapore Expo and Changi Exhibition Centre as a public-private partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As we go about tackling this crisis, we see also many shining examples of SG United in action, like how we went about setting up very quickly Community Care Facilities at the Singapore Expo and the Changi Exhibition Centre – truly, a public-private partnership at work.

sections.label: Societal divides and resilience
sections.summary: Societal divides and inequalities may sharpen in others, but a few will emerge stronger, more united and more resilient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Societal divides and inequalities may sharpen in others.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But a few will emerge from this stronger, more united and more resilient than before.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme payouts
sections.summary: In April, over $7 billion were paid to employers through the Jobs Support Scheme to co-fund wages of over 1.9 million local employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In April, over $7 billion were paid out to employers through the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will help co-fund wages of over 1.9 million local employees.

sections.label: Employer rebates totalling $675 million
sections.summary: By May, over 62,000 employers would have received rebates totalling $675 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By May, over 62,000 employers would have received rebates totalling $675 million.

sections.label: Workfare Special Payment cash support
sections.summary: 400,000 workers will get an extra $3,000 each in cash support through the Workfare Special Payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, 400,000 workers will get extra $3,000 each in cash support through the Workfare Special Payment.

sections.label: SEP Income Relief Scheme payouts
sections.summary: The SEP Income Relief Scheme is expected to pay close to $1 billion to over 100,000 SEPs, with the first payment in end of May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This time round, the Government has made a special effort to also support freelancers and self-employed persons (SEPs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We expect the SEP Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) to pay out close to $1 billion of cash support to over 100,000 SEPs, with the first payment in end of May.

sections.label: Public sector job placements and hiring incentive
sections.summary: The public sector partnered with NTUC's Job Security Council, unions and employers to place over 3,000 individuals, and employers can receive a hiring incentive of 20% salary support capped at $6,000 over six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The public sector has taken the lead to partner NTUC's Job Security Council at e2i, unions and employers to place more than 3,000 individuals from affected sectors to take on jobs such as safe distancing ambassadors and care ambassadors, in various hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Through the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support package, employers can also receive a hiring incentive which provides 20% salary support, capped at $6,000 over six months.

sections.label: Training allowance and traineeship opportunities
sections.summary: The Government funds 80% of the monthly training allowance for up to 12 months, and more than 4,000 traineeship opportunities are offered by 280 organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government funds 80% of the monthly training allowance for up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our young people are absolutely critical to our future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are now more than 4,000 traineeship opportunities offered by 280 organisations.

sections.label: Applications to return processed
sections.summary: In total, about 80,000 applications to return were processed but only a minority could be approved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In total, we processed about 80,000 applications to return but could only approve a minority.

sections.label: Staff deployed for migrant workers
sections.summary: Nearly 3,000 staff, including private sector recruits, are deployed to look after migrant workers' health and well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Including the private sector recruits that supplement our efforts, nearly 3,000 staff are now deployed to look after the health and well-being of our migrant workers.

sections.label: Catered meals and worker testing
sections.summary: More than 10 million catered meals were served, and over 10,000 essential services workers were moved out and progressively tested.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: More than 10 million catered meals have been served.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: More than 10,000 workers in essential services were moved out and progressively tested so they can continue to work safely.

sections.label: WiFi and SIM cards distributed
sections.summary: WiFi access was provided and nearly 300,000 SIM cards distributed so workers can keep in touch with family and friends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, we provided WiFi access and distributed nearly 300,000 SIM cards so the workers can keep in touch with family and friends.

sections.label: SHN extended to four weeks
sections.summary: Excluding workers already in dormitories, the requirement put another 100,000 workers out of circulation, and SHN was extended from two to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Excluding the workers already in dormitories, this requirement put another 100,000 workers out of circulation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To decisively break the cycle of transmission, the SHN was extended from the initial two weeks to four weeks in total.

sections.label: Pulse oximeters for workers
sections.summary: There are plans to issue pulse oximeters and require workers to take readings regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, we plan to issue pulse oximeters and require the workers to take readings regularly.

sections.label: 400,000 migrant workers looked after
sections.summary: Altogether, they are looking after about 400,000 migrant workers, bigger than the size of two Ang Mo Kio GRCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Altogether, they are looking after about 400,000 migrant workers, bigger than the size of two Ang Mo Kio GRCs.

sections.label: Dates distributed
sections.summary: Over 1.5 tonnes of dates had been distributed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over 1.5 tonnes of dates had been distributed.

sections.label: Workers in dormitories and FCDs
sections.summary: About 200,000 workers are housed in 43 large dormitories and about 95,000 in 1,200 FCDs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, there are about 200,000 workers housed in the 43 large dormitories and about 95,000 housed in 1,200 FCDs.

sections.label: Quarantine rooms in dormitories
sections.summary: In early February, MOM asked all FEDA-licensed dormitories to each set aside at least 10 quarantine rooms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In early February, MOM asked all FEDA-licensed dormitories to each put aside at least 10 quarantine rooms.

sections.label: MOM dormitory inspectors and inspections
sections.summary: MOM has about 100 full-time dormitory inspectors, who last year conducted 1,200 inspections and 3,000 investigations across all housing types.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MOM alone has about 100 dormitory inspectors, full-time, who work under the supervision of the Commissioner for Foreign Employee Dormitories, two Deputy Commissioners and eight Assistant Commissioners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year, these officers conducted 1,200 inspections and 3,000 investigations across all housing types.

sections.label: FEDA and EFMA penalties
sections.summary: Under FEDA, dormitory operators can be fined up to $50,000 and/or jailed up to 12 months; under EFMA, employers up to $10,000 and/or 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For offences under FEDA, dormitory operators can be fined up to $50,000 and/or jailed up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, employers can also be fined up to $10,000 and/or jailed up to 12 months.

sections.label: S11 infected workers
sections.summary: S11 is where the highest number of infected workers so far is.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The next one, this is S11 where we have the highest number of infected workers so far.

sections.label: communal living virus transmission
sections.summary: Large numbers of people living together in a communal setting make transmission very likely, as on the US aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt where 950 sailors were infected.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Likewise, when you have a large number of people living together, in a communal setting, there is a very high likelihood of transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There was a significant spread for example on the US aircraft carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, with 950 sailors getting infected within a few weeks.

sections.label: masks and care packs
sections.summary: Temasek Cares distributed re-usable masks and care packs to over 650,000 migrant workers including domestic workers, and Procter & Gamble contributed 300,000 sets of toiletries.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Temasek Cares has mobilised its networks to distribute re-usable masks and care packs to more than 650,000 migrant workers including domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The corporate community is also stepping forward, such as the contribution of 300,000 sets of toiletries by Procter & Gamble.

sections.label: NGOs aid migrant workers
sections.summary: The Inter-agency Task Force thanks 10 NGOs and community groups that deliver food, masks and care packs to migrant workers outside the 43 large dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Inter-agency Task Force (ITF) is especially thankful to a group of 10 NGOs and community groups. such as the Alliance of Guest Workers Outreach, COVID-19 Migrant Support Coalition – which was introduction from Mr Louis Ng; we are very grateful for that – and also Crisis Relief Alliance.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These NGOs and community groups deliver food, masks and care packs to migrant workers outside the 43 large dormitories who may not be getting enough support from their employers.

sections.label: responsibility to migrant workers
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore has a responsibility to migrant workers, appreciates their contributions and sacrifices, and will do everything within its means to help them fight COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: His words are not fanciful but they remind us what this is about: doing our best for each other in times of hardship.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have said right from the beginning that we have a responsibility to our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Many of them made personal sacrifices to come to Singapore to work and they have made significant contributions which we appreciate deeply.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will do everything within our means to make sure that they too win the fight against COVID-19 and reunite with their families in time to come.

sections.label: TCM halls reopen 5 May
sections.summary: From 5 May, Chinese medical halls with a resident TCM practitioner may operate again, but Singaporeans are disappointed that practitioners can only do acupuncture, not tuina and cupping.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, tomorrow is 5 May, Chinese medical halls with a resident TCM practitioner are allowed to operate again.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans are very happy to hear that and I would like to thank the Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, when Singaporeans found out that the TCM practitioners can only do acupuncture, not tuina and cupping, they are very disappointed.

sections.label: ICU number correction and TCM rules
sections.summary: The speaker corrects the ICU patient number from 28 to 22 and says TCM rules were relaxed to allow acupuncture and medicine halls with resident practitioners to open and sell retail products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But before I answer her questions, can I just make a correction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I mentioned in my earlier statement that we have 28 patients in ICU currently and the number is wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We currently have 22 patients in our ICU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For the Traditional Chinese Medicine, we have always allowed some operation of the Traditional Chinese Medicine clinics to attend to chronic diseases and to attend to urgent cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But we have further relaxed some of these rules to allow acupuncture and to also allow medicine halls, which have resident Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners there, to allow the medicine hall to be open and able to sell retail products, particularly the Traditional Chinese Medicine products in these shops, for the convenience of residents in general.

sections.label: Additional support discussions with agencies
sections.summary: Government is discussing with MTI and MOF whether additional support is needed, and more help will be provided where needed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the meantime, of course, we are in discussion with economic agencies – MTI and, very importantly with MOF – to see if additional support is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat has made the Government's position very clear; and that is, where more help is needed, it will be provided.

sections.label: No plan to test all foreign workers
sections.summary: Currently, there is no plan to test all foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Currently, we do not plan to test all foreign workers.

sections.label: Raising testing capacity to 40,000
sections.summary: Testing capacity is being progressively raised from about 8,000 per day, with hope to reach 40,000 soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, there are infrastructure and manpower requirements at every stage of the test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are progressively raising the capacity and we hope to reach 40,000 as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Today, we are able to do about 8,000 per day and we hope that in a short period of time, we will be able to reach 40,000 soon.

sections.label: Local production and F&B HBBs
sections.summary: Minister was asked for an update on local production capabilities, and F&B related HBBs may restart on 12 May with sufficient supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And related to that, we spoke at the last Sitting on upping local production capabilities for some of this equipment, could the Minister update the House on the progress on this?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I note that for F&B related HBBs, they will be allowed to restart on 12 May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Currently, we have sufficient supplies, but we should not take this for granted.

sections.label: Food provision and remdesivir development
sections.summary: With fewer cases, less medical supplies are consumed; food outlets, home-based provision, delivery and take-out are permitted, and remdesivir was approved by the US FDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Once we have a lower number of cases, then we will consume less of our medical supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, in providing food for Singaporeans, whether it is a physical outlet or it is a home-based provision, then you can do so, and delivery and take-out is permitted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the United States, there has been development on the potential COVID-19 treatment known as the remdesivir.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And it has been approved by the US FDA and the company has announced it will donate the first 140,000 doses in May to hospitals in the United States and around the world.

sections.label: Allocation of drug for trial
sections.summary: As part of the trial, Singapore gets a certain allocation of the drug for testing and treatment of patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As part of the trial, we get certain allocation of this drug for testing and treatment of our patients.

sections.label: Care for infected migrant workers
sections.summary: An infected migrant worker will receive the same good care as a Singaporean until full recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If a migrant worker is infected, we will make sure that he receives the same good care as a Singaporean until full recovery.

sections.label: Dorm medical teams and inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether mental health professionals and psychological services will be added to dorm medical teams, and whether a Commission of Inquiry will be appointed later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I also understand that for all the 43 purpose-built dorms (PBDs), there is already an on-site medical team in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, is the Minister planning to mandate that within this medical team, that there would be at least a mental health professional in the form of a counsellor or a psychologist with the medical team?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is the Minister looking to also include psychological services through these teleconsultation support?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I agree with Minister Lawrence Wong that this is clearly a colossal task at hand, so it is not the time to look into a review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But would the Ministers assure Singapore and our migrant workers that a Commission of Inquiry would be appointed when we are out of the eye of the storm and when that would be likely, so that we can be committed to making the structural changes needed and be better prepared for the next epidemic or pandemic.

sections.label: Committed to post-crisis review
sections.summary: The speaker says he explicitly stated in his speech that a comprehensive review will be done after the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I am somewhat puzzled by it because the question almost presupposes that we do not want to do a review despite me saying explicitly in my speech just now that we want to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think if you heard my speech just now, I said that we are committed to doing a comprehensive review after the crisis.

sections.label: Worker demands and dorm space
sections.summary: The speaker says no migrant worker has demanded an apology, and describes the current 4.5 sqm space including kitchen, dining and toilet areas.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These are the things that they have asked of us.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I have not come across one single migrant worker himself who has demanded an apology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the current 4.5 sqm – which, if you break it down, is about 2.1 by 2.1 metres and that includes the kitchen, the dining and the toilet areas.

sections.label: Culturing virus after 14 days
sections.summary: The test cannot conclusively determine whether fragments are viable viruses, and scientists find culturing difficult usually after 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The test is not able to determine conclusively whether these are fragments or viable viruses, but when the scientists try to culture this virus, they find it very difficult to culture them after a certain number of days – usually after 14 days.

sections.label: Discharge talks and address updates
sections.summary: Discussions with infectious disease experts continue on helping patients be discharged, and worker address updates through OFWAS are not as prompt as desired.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, I think these are some things that we are looking and discussing with the infectious disease experts' community to see how we can come to some way to helping these patients so that they can be discharged and go home.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We keep track of the workers' whereabouts or where they live through the Online Foreign Worker Address Service (OFWAS).

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Sometimes, the workers move from one place to another at the request of their employers or if they have found new accommodation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, I must say that this updating is not as prompt as we would like it to be.

sections.label: Seeking medical care during pandemic
sections.summary: Singaporeans are encouraged to seek medical care when needed, and no signs seen of patients staying away despite heart attack or stroke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We want to encourage Singaporeans to continue to seek medical care when the situation arises, when they need to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So far, we have not seen signs of patients who are staying away despite having a heart attack or stroke.

sections.label: Support for medical support staff
sections.summary: Support provided goes beyond medical professionals to support staff, including counselling sessions, supervisors talking to them and support groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The support that we provide goes beyond just medical professionals, but also the support staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And much of this support includes counselling sessions, supervisors talking to them as well as ways for them to seek help, including support groups within the work spaces.

sections.label: Testing sewage question
sections.summary: A question asks Minister Gan whether the Ministry is looking at testing sewage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To Minister Gan, firstly, in terms of testing, is the Ministry looking at testing sewage?

sections.label: Testing close contacts commitment
sections.summary: A question asks whether all close contacts of a confirmed COVID-19 case will be tested as capacity is ramped up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is there going to be a commitment to test all of the people who are close contacts of a confirmed COVID-19 case going forward since our capacity is being ramped up?

sections.label: Vaccine availability thinking
sections.summary: A question asks what MOH's thinking is about when a vaccine might be available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is MOH's thinking right now about when we might see a vaccine available?

sections.label: Sewage testing trials
sections.summary: Trials are being done to pick up virus fragments from sewage to assess a vicinity such as dormitory, nursing home, hospital or housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In fact, we are doing trials to see whether we can pick up fragments of the virus from the sewage to allow us to have an assessment whether a particular vicinity, whether it is a dormitory, nursing home or hospital – in a hospital, probably you find a lot, because there are a lot of patients there who are infected with the COVID-19 – or housing estates if they have outbreaks.

sections.label: Ramping up testing capacity
sections.summary: Testing capacity is being ramped up, with hopes to first test all prolonged ARI cases to detect more cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Testing capacity, yes, we are ramping up and we are hoping to, first, test all prolonged ARI cases, those with prolonged acute respiratory symptoms so that we are able to detect more cases.

sections.label: Targeted testing strategy expansion
sections.summary: Testing strategy may need to be targeted, with plans to expand to cover all PARI and ramp up for ARI cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But to be effective in case finding, we may need to be quite targeted in our testing strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we are planning to expand it to cover all PARI and, hopefully, we are able to ramp up somewhat for the ARI cases in a more targeted way.

sections.label: Vaccine not immediate solution
sections.summary: From testing to approval for population use is still some way off, so the vaccine cannot solve immediate community infection challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But from here to testing, to eventually being approved for use by the population, I think there is still some way off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I think we cannot count on the vaccine to solve our immediate challenges of infection cases in the community.

sections.label: Prioritising older migrant workers testing
sections.summary: Reports suggest resource constraints mean prioritising testing and isolation of older migrant workers and essential services workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Reports suggest that due to resource constraints, we are prioritising testing of and isolation of older migrant workers because of the higher health risks as well as essential services workers.

sections.label: Medical care for dormitory workers
sections.summary: Symptomatic dormitory workers are assessed, given medical care, and older or serious cases sent to hospitals for testing and treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For the foreign workers in the dormitories, whenever they have symptoms, we assess them and the key priority is to make sure that all the workers in the dormitories receive appropriate medical care to make sure that they are taken care of, their illnesses are treated and, if they are at risk of serious or deteriorating conditions, particularly for the older workers, we take them out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Most of these workers who are older or who have more serious conditions, will be sent to hospitals and when they arrive in hospitals, they will be tested and they will be given appropriate treatment based on their test outcomes.

sections.label: TraceTogether app take-up rate
sections.summary: A supplementary question concerns leveraging technology for aggressive tracing, noting the TraceTogether app take-up rate is about 17%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My supplementary question is on the issue of leveraging technology for aggressive tracing – a topic that the hon Ministers, Mr Gan Kim Yong and Mr Lawrence Wong touched on in their Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand that the take-up rate for the TraceTogether app is about 17%, which is relatively low.

sections.label: Enhancing TraceTogether app for iOS
sections.summary: The first priority is to enhance the TraceTogether app, particularly for use with iOS phones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have mentioned just now, our first priority now is to enhance the TraceTogether app, particularly in use with the iOS phone.

sections.label: New Zealand RE and lockdown easing
sections.summary: New Zealand's Prime Minister said lockdown measures could be eased because the virus RE fell from 2 to 0.48.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, the New Zealand Prime Minister told her country that they were able to ease their lockdown measures because the RE of the virus in New Zealand had gone from 2 to 0.48, meaning that a person is likely to infect less than one other person at that particular time.

sections.label: Dormitory transmission origins and recovery
sections.summary: The exact origin of dormitory transmission is unknown and will not be speculated on; the focus is control, recovery and preventing recurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I think we need to take into account all the factors in order for us to be able to restore some of the activities safely.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think the short answer to her question is, no, we do not exactly know how the transmission in the dormitories got started.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We also do not want to speculate about its exact origins because it is not helpful to risk any group within the dormitories being targeted for blame.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The important thing right now is that it has happened.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have to try and bring it under control and then we have to focus on getting ourselves onto the recovery path.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Very importantly, we also want to set our sights on how a recurrence can be prevented.

sections.label: TCM medical halls and chronic patients
sections.summary: Chronic patients have always been allowed to buy medicine from medical halls, and halls with resident TCM practitioners may now serve other customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For chronic patients, we have always allowed them to purchase medicine from the medical halls when they consult the TCM practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have now actually liberalised it and we allow medical halls which have resident TCM practitioners to open, to be able to serve other customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But we will continue to look at whether we can liberalise it further.

sections.label: Task force debate on TCM liberalisation
sections.summary: The task force had the same debate, and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's feedback will be taken seriously in considering further liberalisation for TCM practitioners and medical halls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I must say that we had the same debate in the task force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is not an easy decision, but I will take Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's feedback seriously – I always take her feedback very seriously – and we will look at whether or not we could further liberalise for TCM practitioners, including the medical halls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But, today, medical halls that have a resident TCM practitioner are already allowed to do so.

sections.label: Opening medical halls to other buyers
sections.summary: Previously only the TCM practitioner's patient could buy from the hall, but now other people may purchase there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Previously, we only allowed the patient whom the TCM practitioner had seen to purchase from the hall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Now, we have opened the hall to other people who can purchase from these halls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I propose to heed Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's advice and seek more nutrition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 6.20 pm.
